record.title: OpenAI reports an automated Linux pipeline that reproduced 1,724 kernel vulnerabilities and developed patches for 948 unique LPEs
record.summary: OpenAI describes a controlled prototype that scanned selected Linux kernel audit targets using an upcoming cyber model and agent pipeline. In its mid-October run, it reports 2,308 candidate findings, 1,724 dynamically reproduced vulnerabilities, 291 information-leak proofs of concept, 1,169 working LPE exploits and 948 distinct patches corresponding to 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities. OpenAI reports about USD 1.21 million in API-credit cost. OpenAI also reports that human review caught 20 wrong-vulnerability attributions among 200 apparent successes in an early run, after which it added an independent path check. The page itself is internally inconsistent: its overview and findings summary say 948 LPE exploits, while the detailed section reports 1,169 working exploits and 948 distinct patches. These remain first-party results from one workflow: independent reproduction, maintainer acceptance of all patches, transfer beyond the tested configurations and generalized security impact are not established.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published a technical account on 4 November 2026 describing a prototype for Linux kernel vulnerability discovery, dynamic validation, exploitability assessment and patch generation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that a mid-October run identified 2,308 candidate findings in selected Linux kernel targets, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, generated 291 information-leak proofs of concept and 1,169 working local privilege-escalation exploits, then developed 948 distinct patches corresponding to 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities after variant analysis.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports about USD 1.21 million in API-credit cost for the described run and says its audit targets covered about 7% of the kernel codebase; these figures apply to its stated prototype, target configuration and workflow.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected account does not establish independent reproduction, maintainer acceptance of the generated patches, equivalent results on other kernels or threat models, or a general AI vulnerability-discovery rate.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports that an early run counted 200 successful local privilege escalations, but human review found 20 reached root through a different zero-day than the assigned vulnerability; it says the later workflow tightened constraints and added an independent check that each final exploit used its assigned vulnerability.

claims.label: DISPUTED
claims.text: The same OpenAI page is internally inconsistent about the count: its overview and findings summary say 948 working LPE exploits, while the detailed exploitability section reports 1,169 working LPE exploits and 948 distinct patches, using 948 to count unique LPE vulnerabilities. The report does not reconcile this difference.

contradictory_evidence: The same OpenAI page is internally inconsistent about the count: its overview and findings summary say 948 working LPE exploits, while the detailed exploitability section reports 1,169 working LPE exploits and 948 distinct patches, using 948 to count unique LPE vulnerabilities. The report does not reconcile this difference.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the counts, exploitability assessments, patch correctness or reported cost was reviewed.
The account reports 1,169 working LPE exploits and 948 distinct patches but does not provide a per-finding public mapping in the inspected page.
Results and cost are from one provider-reported workflow on selected targets and do not establish performance or economics across kernels, models or threat models.

The report identifies 20 wrong-vulnerability attributions among 200 early apparent successes and describes a subsequent independent path check, but does not expose a per-finding public audit sufficient to independently measure final attribution error.
OpenAI’s overview/summary says 948 working LPE exploits, but its detailed section reports 1,169 working exploits and 948 distinct patches; the source does not reconcile its count wording.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated under the stated threat model, the reported scale of dynamically validated kernel vulnerabilities and generated local privilege-escalation exploits could materially change defensive audit capacity and patching priorities. The score reflects consequence, not truth or generality of one provider-reported run.
limitations: All capability, count, cost and comparative figures are first-party claims from OpenAI.
The full-kernel prototype targeted selected audit regions, which OpenAI says covered about 7% of the kernel codebase.
The report says human researchers reviewed and reported outputs; it does not establish that every generated patch was accepted or merged.
A single provider-reported run does not estimate general vulnerability-discovery rates or attack prevalence.

OpenAI says an early workflow produced 20 false-success exploit attributions among 200 apparent successes; the report describes a later control change, but independent validation of that control and the final attribution accuracy was not reviewed.

The same OpenAI page reports 948 working LPE exploits in its overview/summary but 1,169 working exploits and 948 distinct patches in its detailed section; this internal count inconsistency is unresolved.

OpenAI also reports that human review caught 20 wrong-vulnerability attributions among 200 apparent successes in an early run, after which it added an independent path check. technical.claimed_result: OpenAI reports 2,308 deduplicated candidate findings, 1,724 dynamic reproductions, 291 information-leak proofs of concept, 1,169 working local privilege-escalation exploits and 948 distinct patches corresponding to 948 unique LPE vulnerabilities in the mid-October run. The page overview/summary instead says 948 working LPE exploits; the detailed exploitability section says 1,169 working exploits and 948 distinct patches. The source does not reconcile these counts.
technical.compute_or_cost: OpenAI reports approximately USD 1.213 million in API credits for the mid-October full-kernel-prototype run; a separate adapted kernelCTF campaign is reported at approximately USD 32,936. These are provider-reported costs for its models, workflow and targets.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary source demonstrates that OpenAI published these methods and reported results; it does not independently establish the run outputs.
technical.mechanism: Scout agents select reachable, security-relevant audit targets; analyst agents generate candidate findings; validation agents attempt dynamic reproduction in isolated VMs; exploit-development agents test impact with standard-distribution protections enabled; patch generation includes variant analysis; human researchers review reports and patches before reporting. OpenAI says an early run misattributed 20 of 200 apparent root-shell successes to vulnerabilities other than the assigned finding; it reports adding tighter task constraints and an independent check of each exploit path.
technical.regime: Provider-reported controlled research prototype on selected Linux kernel targets, including a stock desktop OS configuration and an adapted kernelCTF environment. One full-run report is dated mid-October 2026.
technical.reproducibility: No independent reproduction or full public reproduction package was inspected. The report says a human review of an early run caught 20 wrong-vulnerability attributions among 200 apparent successes and that the later workflow added an independent attribution check; independent validation of that control remains open.
technical.strongest_baseline: OpenAI compares the newer-model run with a July GPT-5.6 Sol run and reports more than five times as many novel LPEs despite three months of hardening; the comparison is provider-reported and the inspected account does not establish a matched independent evaluation.

brief.title: OpenAI reports an automated Linux pipeline that reproduced 1,724 kernel vulnerabilities and developed patches for 948 unique LPEs
brief.why_it_matters: If independently reproduced, this pipeline could expand the volume of kernel security findings defenders can validate and remediate. The report also shows that candidate triage, dynamic validation, exploitation assessment and patch review remain separate costly stages. The report’s own early false-success episode shows why exploit-path attribution must be checked separately from obtaining root. Its measured scale and cost are specific to one provider-reported run, so it does not establish a general discovery rate or cost advantage.
